messages:
incident-bot: PAGER -> SEV2: Elevated p99 tail latency for streaming responses in eu-west2. Alert threshold breached for 12m. Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream, /v1/generate

oncall-sre: ack. I'm paged and on it. tagging @maria.g and @network-eng for routing checks.

maria.g: seeing p95 ~ 370ms, p99 ~ 2.7s from synthetic probes. Customer reports: intermittent stalls during streaming, some clients retrying.

neil.k: adding logs — I'm seeing a lot of TCP retransmits at the NAT hop in eu-west2-a -> eu-west2-b path. Packet loss spikes around 0.8-1.2% for affected subnets.

network-eng: confirming. We're also seeing increased TLS handshake time for new connections: median handshake ~120ms -> 900ms on some nodes. Likely cross-AZ NAT hairpin + ephemeral port exhaustion symptoms.

oncall-sre: good data. Quick checklist: 1) confirm customer impact and SLOs 2) try local mitigation (route pinned to same AZ) 3) if needed shift traffic to eu-west1 fallback 4) coordinate handoff.

support-tilly: several customers report duplicated tokens and stalled streams; support ticket batch #3245 shows 14 customers degraded in last 30m. We should treat as customer-impacting.

ops-lead: @network-eng, can we confirm whether NAT gateway metrics show port exhaustion or queueing? Any active deployment/reconfig around 08:10 UTC?

network-eng: checked NAT pools: ephemeral ports allocation rose sharply 08:06-08:12. Conntrack table shows spike in TIME_WAIT entries. No config change at 08:10. Hypothesis: traffic shift from canary -> all AZs causing burst of new TLS connections to cross-zone endpoints.

oncall-sre: run diagnostics commands pasted below. Please run on eu-west2-a and eu-west2-b edge nodes.

network-eng: running: 
```
# check TLS handshake distribution
ss -tanp | grep ESTAB | wc -l
sudo tcptraceroute -n 10.0.5.1 443
sudo conntrack -L | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l
```

maria.g: also running quick probe from synth cluster: `curl -sv --max-time 10 https://eu-west2.redwood.example/v1/chat/stream` — observing delayed TLS handshake followed by steady token stream once established. When handshake >600ms, client-side streaming window times out and retries.

neil.k: I pushed a short live capture. Key observations: repeated SYN+ACK retries and retransmits between AZ gateways, RTO climbs before TLS handshake completes. Possible queuing on cross-AZ router or NAT device CPU saturation.

oncall-sre: mitigation plan (short term):
- Step A: Pin streaming traffic to same AZ for existing keep-alive connections (reduce cross-AZ hops). Deploy per-route sticky routing for 15m.
- Step B: Reduce new connection churn: enable connection pooling at gateway (keepalive) and increase ephemeral port range on NATs if safe.
- Step C: If network-side mitigation insufficient, fail traffic over to eu-west1 standby for heavy customers.

network-eng: implementing Step A now — toggling routing policy to prefer same-AZ endpoints for existing customers. Rolling change across lb slices, should be non-disruptive. ETA ~ 3 mins.

incident-bot: config-change recorded: routing_policy.update by network-eng at 2724001289.

maria.g: after routing pref change: p95 down to ~220ms, p99 trending down to ~900ms. Some in-flight streams still experiencing stalls until keepalive rebinds.

neil.k: NAT metrics show ephemeral port usage plateauing but still high. We should expand ephemeral range as a safety valve. There is a small risk of breaking older clients; recommend narrow increment and monitor.

ops-lead: approve ephemeral range bump by +2048 ports on nat-proxy set; do a staged increase in eu-west2-a then b. Coordinate with support to watch client errors.

network-eng: applying ephemeral increase on eu-west2-a now. command: `sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="10240 65535"` (already scripted runbook).

oncall-sre: after ephemeral bump: p99 further down to ~520ms. TLS handshake medians back to ~160ms. Packet loss at 0.2% now. Good sign.

support-tilly: customer tickets still trickling but severity reduced. Noticing one large streaming customer still hitting timeouts — investigating their route.

maria.g: tracing indicates that customer's traffic was pinned to eu-west2-b which had higher NAT queue lengths — connection draining caused retries. We're rebalancing their traffic to eu-west2-a where NAT capacity freed.

incident-bot: paging note: paging window open, timestamp 2724001390.

neil.k: running post-mortem probes: `mtr`, `tcpdump` confirms packet retransmits correlated with peak conntrack usage. Looks like the root cause was an unexpected cross-AZ promotion of connection sources during a small canary expansion — created a burst of new TLS connections across NATs causing queueing and handshake tail.

oncall-sre: immediate mitigations completed: routing preference, ephemeral bump, targeted customer rebalancing. Next steps:
- 1) Keep paging window open for 60m monitoring.
- 2) Network team to dig into NAT autoscaling/queueing thresholds. Possible follow-ups: autoscale NAT instances sooner, raise conntrack table size, or add connection-proxying layer to absorb bursts.
- 3) Ops to craft a short customer-facing status blurb if SLOs still degraded.

ops-lead: will schedule an incident follow-up and assign action items. @network-eng you own root cause analysis. @oncall-sre please craft timeline and mitigation log for postmortem.

maria.g: quick note for postmortem: collect the following: netflow around 08:00-08:20, NAT metrics (port allocation, CPU), conntrack dumps, LB routing policy changes, synth probe timeseries, and affected customer list.

support-tilly: prepping status message draft: "We're mitigating elevated streaming latency in eu-west2 caused by cross-AZ NAT queueing leading to longer TLS handshakes. We've applied routing and NAT fixes; customers should see improved behavior. We'll post a full incident report once RCA is complete."

oncall-sre: handoff: I'm going offline for another pager. Handover to @neil.k for monitoring and to @maria.g for followups. If any regression, page incident-bot again.

neil.k: acked. I'll monitor p99/p95 for next 60m, and escalate to oncall if anything over 1.5s.

incident-bot: Handoff logged: previous oncall oncall-sre -> new lead neil.k at 2724001540.

ops-lead: thanks everyone. We'll reconvene for a 30-min postmortem scheduled in #incidents at 09:15 UTC.

support-tilly: posting initial customer blurb now.

maria.g: capturing runbook notes and saving artifacts to /runbooks/incidents/2724001234-wire-bridge.

neil.k: monitoring shows stable metrics now. Closing active mitigations but leaving routing preference for 20m.

oncall-sre: thanks team. Logging final note: root cause likely cross-AZ connection churn causing NAT queuing + conntrack exhaustion -> TLS tail spikes -> client-side stream retries. Follow-ups: improve NAT autoscaling, add connection-proxy to reduce TLS churn, add synth tests targeting handshake percentiles.

incident-bot: Incident updated to MONITORING. All hands: please add any follow-up tickets to the incident thread."
